claims.claim: Canadian health ministers meet in Winnipeg on Oct. 15, 2026, hosted by Manitoba's Uzoma Asagwara, with Michel co-chairing Friday's meeting
Federal Health Minister Marjorie Michel announced on social media late Wednesday a one-year extension of mental health, addictions and home care funding worth $1.2 billion
Provincial and territorial health ministers, meeting with finance counterparts earlier in October, said they were united in calling on Ottawa to be a full funding partner
claims.attributed_to: statement from health ministers via The Canadian Press

claims.claim: Health ministers warned of 'profound and negative' effects on patients and health-care jobs if the agreements were not renewed

$4.8 billion over four years for home care, community care and mental health and addiction services ends March 2027; $3 billion for long-term care safety sunsets in 2026; $1.7 billion for PSW wages pays out by 2028
The 2023 federal budget pledged $200 billion in additional health funding over 10 years
The Canada Health Transfer grows five per cent a year until 2028, then a minimum three per cent; premiers say the five per cent floor must hold
Manitoba Health Minister Uzoma Asagwara said 'I feel Minister Michel has been listening'
claims.attributed_to: Uzoma Asagwara via The Canadian Press

claims.claim: Newfoundland and Labrador Health Minister Joedy Wall said Humberwood expansion and Corner Brook long-term beds will not be affected if funding is not renewed
CMA and nurses' unions jointly called for CHT and bilateral agreement certainty and urged ministers to press for passage of Bill S-5 and Bill C-34
Finance Minister Champagne committed to continuing discussions on immediate funding pressures and long-term health system sustainability after meeting provincial and territorial finance ministers
Health Canada renewed the Working Together bilateral agreement with the Northwest Territories, $51.2 million over seven years, the first in a series of renewals

The full text and duration of Michel's announcement beyond the one-year, $1.2-billion figure, whether all three funding streams are covered at existing levels, and when other bilateral renewals will be announced are not established
